text:
ops-bot: Incident alert — dedicated pool eu-west-1 | SLO p99 spike >6s, streaming stalls detected, queue_depth=432, warmup_pending≈120s, autoscaler_delay≈45s. Paging policy SLO-1 triggered :rotating_light: (1754242424)
maria: investigating. metrics show p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~6.4s, streaming_stalls=78 over last 5m
sam: grabbing autoscaler logs now. seeing repeated warmup handshakes failing, backoff kicks in
lee: is this across all dedicated pools or one hotshot pool?
maria: concentrated on pool-dedicated-eu-w1-hotshot, other pools normal
kevin: any 5xxs or just high latency/stalls? customers reporting errors?
prod-support: multiple customers reporting streaming timeouts. Acme Inc reporting degraded chat sessions & some dropped streams when queue >200
carla: opening an on-call bridge and paging @oncall. plan: manual mitigation + triage
oncall: acked, joining. please post bridge link and short summary
sam: quick summary: autoscaler attempted scale but new nodes didn't register due to KV/handshake timeouts during warmup; autoscaler backoff prevented further attempts for ~40s window
maria: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) route latency-sensitive streaming to fallback region (eu-east-1) 2) temporarily increase hotshot pool target by +3 3) relax handshake timeout to allow KV sync during warmup
kevin: I'll manually bump the pool target: running `rctl scale pool-dedicated-eu-w1-hotshot --add 3`
kevin: scale request submitted, jobs id=98765,98766,98767
ops-bot: Autoscaler event: scale_up_request accepted id=67890 (timestamp 1754242450)
sam: watching registration logs: `grep warmup /var/log/autoscaler.log` -> repeated `Handshake timeout waiting for KV cache` and `registration failed: preflight_kv_miss`
maria: to buy time we can flip runtime flag to relax handshake: `handshake.timeout=60s` on pool config (temporary)
carla: risk? slower failure detection but allows nodes to register and start serving sooner—ok to proceed for mitigation
kevin: applied runtime flag via admin API -> 200 OK, change propagated to pool controller
prod-support: updating customer comms: status page note -> "Degraded streaming performance in eu-west-1 due to capacity warmup delays; mitigation in progress."
maria: routing rule created: divert priority streaming traffic to eu-east fallback model variant (small-stream-fallback) for impacted orgs
lee: monitoring: p99 down from 6.4s -> ~3.1s after routing + scale ops; streaming stalls reduced to 12 in last 2m
carla: queue_depth now 180 and trending down. keep an eye on registration success rate and KV sync metrics
kevin: registration events for new nodes: node-98765 registered at 1754242512, node-98766 registered at 1754242515, node-98767 registered at 1754242520
sam: seeing fewer handshake failures after timeout relax. autoscaler backoff window cleared and no additional rejection occurs
oncall: customer impact matrix: Acme Inc (chat) ~30% degraded requests, others minor. Escalated one account to SE due to SLA concern. Notifying account team
maria: post-mitigation checklist: 1) keep fallback route for 30m 2) monitor p99 <2s and queue <50 for 10m 3) collect logs for RCA
kevin: quick log snippet from runtime: ```ERROR runtime/kv.go:127 handshake timeout: waiting for shard 12```
sam: probable root: a race in warmup path where KV partitions not yet available when node registers => registration fails => autoscaler sees failed warmup and backs off. Need to make registration idempotent and surface registration success metric to alerts
carla: working timeline: - 1754242424 alert - 1754242450 scale request accepted - 1754242512 first node registered - 1754242580 p99 improved but queue still elevated - 1754242700 queue <200 - 1754242720 criteria for closing bridge in sight
prod-support: customers notified via status page and via direct messages to impacted accounts. Seeding interim mitigation steps in customer emails (retry guidance + fallback region)
oncall: handing off to night oncall @sam for monitoring and RCA follow-up. attaching runbook: https://go/runbooks/dedicated-warmup (internal)
sam: ack, I'll run postmortem checklist, capture autoscaler backoff curve and KV partition telemetry, and propose immediate fix (increase registration retries + expose success metric)
maria: long-term actions: 1) lower autoscaler punitive backoff for warmup failures 2) add canary warmup test that validates KV availability before autoscaler counts node as failed 3) alert on registration_success_rate dropping below 95%
kevin: collecting additional logs for PM: `tail -n 100 /var/log/serving/runtime.log | grep -i "handshake"` saved to s3://redwood-incidents/1754242424/logs
carla: thanks all. criteria for closing bridge: p99 < 2s and queue_depth < 50 sustained for 10m. leaving notes in the incident ticket. updating runbook with temporary handshake flag used for mitigation
ops-bot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV-2 and bridge closed at 1754242724 :white_check_mark:"
